I'm checking each claim against the evidence. The root cause reads as a hedged F1 finding, and the plain-words version is marked "likely," which F1 and P1 support. The risk is that totals could keep falling while the feature stays on, and totals already short stay wrong until someone repairs them. Downstream monthly statements and per-item spend averages that depend on those totals could show shoppers incorrect figures.

I'm working through each claim in the chain and checking it against the cited sources. The causal chain's second step is stated as fact, but its mechanism traces back to the F1 finding, so I'll accept it. The third step is where I'm checking carefully: the recording-path change, the timing against the oldest affected purchase, and whether any deploy or earlier change was actually ruled out.

I'm checking the remaining contributing factors and the went-wrong rows against the record: the weekly check that never fired, the absence of any derive-path test, and the Slack post that nobody was paged about. Each reads as supported, so I'll move on to finalize the table rows.

supported.quote: With monthly-spend-feature on, `record_a_purchase` in `src/io_shop/purchase_ledger.py` records each purchase through `record_purchase_deriving_the_month`, which adds the purchase to `purchases` and moves `total_cents` but never writes `total_this_month_cents`.
Each shopper's stored month total therefore stays where it was while their this-month purchases grow, and falls further below their sum with every purchase.
It rests on F1, a reading of the source nothing ran, so it is unverified.

After a feature setting was switched on, the shop likely began recording each purchase without adding it to the shopper's stored running total for the month, so those stored totals fell behind what shoppers had actually bought.
While monthly-spend-feature stayed on, shoppers' stored month totals could keep falling further behind with every purchase
the totals already short stay wrong until someone rewrites them
the monthly statements and per-item spend averages that read those totals could show shoppers the wrong figures
Shoppers' stored spend totals fell short of the purchases behind them
The stored spend totals of the shoppers checked no longer matched the purchases behind them, falling short of what had been bought, starting from purchases recorded at the onset.
A shopper's stored month total did not grow as their purchases were recorded, so it fell below the sum of their this-month purchase prices, which is what the reconciliation compares it with.
Purchases began going through a different recording path when admin switched on the feature flag monthly-spend-feature at {P1.1}, shortly before the oldest affected purchase.
No deploy came back for the window searched.
No earlier change was ruled out: no metrics from before the onset were read, and nothing else in the record shows the service healthy with an earlier change in place.
rows: Error rate: not measured by the metrics - metrics were read, but none from the hour before the onset

supported.quote: With the flag on, purchases are recorded through a path that, by Code-Fix's reading, does not update the stored month total.
The spend-integrity check that found the fault runs only every {A5} days, and no other check comparing stored month totals with purchases was seen.
Before monthly-spend-feature was switched on, no test or check was seen confirming that the flag-on purchase path keeps the stored month total in line with the purchases.
By Code-Fix's account, the derive-path cases it adds would fail against the old code.
Nobody was paged: the alert was linked to no on-call incident, so the recommended revert and the repair waited on someone noticing.
